name: Purify water
summary: Filter out the dirt first, then kill germs by boiling, chlorine, UV or sunlight. Under-sink reverse osmosis units, fridge filters and office water coolers hold good filters nobody thinks to take. Pool supply stores hold calcium hypochlorite (pool shock), which treats far more water per kilo than bleach. Activated carbon removes taste and some chemicals but does not kill germs.

parts.why: Strips sediment; a filter rated absolute 1 micron or finer stops Giardia cysts (HealthLinkBC 10). An RO unit is not a germ treatment, so still disinfect (Pentair RO-2550)
Kills germs in clear water: plain bleach or pool shock
Removes taste, smell and some chemicals after filtering
UV-C kills germs in clear water with little power
Raised containers for a gravity filter
Plumbing for gravity and pumped filters
Pushes water through an RO membrane, which needs pressure

tips: Boiling always works on germs: a rolling boil for 1 minute, or at least 2 minutes above 2,000 m (Health Canada BWA). It doesn't remove nitrate and can raise it (Health Canada BWA): well water that may hold nitrate needs a test before it goes into a baby's formula (AHS nitrate).

Plain unscented bleach: about 2 drops per litre of clear water, then wait 30 minutes (CDC). If the water is still cloudy or colder than 10 °C (50 °F), use 4 drops and wait 1 to 2 hours, covered (HealthLinkBC 49b). It should smell faintly of chlorine.
Use only plain chlorine. Pool tablets with stabiliser or algaecide are not for drinking water.

Chlorine does not kill Cryptosporidium (Health Canada protozoa) and is generally not effective against Giardia (HealthLinkBC 10). For lake, river and pond water, boil it or use a cyst-rated filter, absolute 1 micron or finer (HealthLinkBC 10), then add chlorine to protect it in storage (Sphere).

In full sun for 6 hours or more (2 days if cloudy), clear bottles of clear water cut bacteria and Giardia; Cryptosporidium and most viruses fall only in ideal conditions (CDC Yellow Book, Eawag manual). Best at latitudes 15° to 35° (SSWM SODIS): in a Canadian winter, boil or chlorinate instead.
Filter cloudy water before using chlorine or UV: dirt shields germs. An RO unit doesn't replace disinfection either: Pentair says to disinfect before or after its unit (Pentair RO-2550).
